title: A robot with a discriminated union
description:
A robot starts at `(0, 0)` facing north and follows commands:

```typescript
type Command =
  | { kind: "move"; steps: number }
  | { kind: "turn"; direction: "left" | "right" }
  | { kind: "say"; text: string };

function run(commands: Command[]): { x: number; y: number; facing: string; log: string[] }
function isCommand(x: unknown): x is Command
function parseProgram(json: string): Command[]
```

- `move` goes `steps` squares in the facing direction: north is `y + 1`, east `x + 1`, south `y - 1`, west `x - 1`.
- `turn` turns 90 degrees; the facings are `"north"`, `"east"`, `"south"`, `"west"`.
- `say` adds `"(<x>, <y>): <text>"` to the log.
- `isCommand` checks an unknown value really is one of the three variants with the right property types (`steps` a number, `direction` exactly `"left"` or `"right"`, `text` a string).
- `parseProgram` parses JSON text that must be an array, and returns only the elements that pass `isCommand`.

Use a `switch` on `kind` with an exhaustive `never` check in `run`.
hints: In each `case`, TypeScript narrows `c` to that variant, so `c.steps` is only allowed under `"move"`.
Turning right is `+1` around the list of four facings and left is `+3` (the same as `-1`), both `% 4`.
rules: Make isCommand a type guard: x is Command.
Use a never check so every command kind is handled.
Use a switch on the command's kind.
